implementation.scheduler: Every ten minutes, one fixed authenticated POST {} to /api/workspace-billing-background; three-second request timeout. Only 202 is an accepted invocation. No inline Stripe call and no immediate retry after unknown dispatch.
implementation.background: Existing workspace_billing records and workspace_billing_cursor/active cursor only. One conditional lease, at most three visited records, four-minute wave provider deadline and 45 seconds per record. Five-second Stripe request timeout includes response JSON; financial mutations require at least five seconds remaining.
implementation.ownership: Current cursor lease, workspace incarnation, original Checkout identity, merchant/mode and unchanged configured key checked before and after each background provider response. Current renewal claim also fences ordinary owner actions. A late old wave cannot release a newer lease or advance its cursor.
implementation.identity: Existing original Checkout, subscription and idempotency keys retained. Lost applied renewal mutations reconcile by canonical GET without another POST. A still-unapplied mutation reuses its identity; a23-hour identity rotation requires canonical verification under the same retained renewal claim.
implementation.fairness: Cursor advances for each visited valid, invalid or failed record. Expired process-death wave/renewal claims are repaired by the next scheduled invocation. No new job store, queue, worker key or provider framework.
implementation.observability: health/workspaceBilling:lastDispatch is invocation acceptance only. health/workspaceBilling:lastRun is completed recovery; unresolved Checkout or renewal states are unconfirmed, never a healthy financial completion. A monotonic generation in that same cursor orders completed health even if separate waves share the exact millisecond timestamp.
implementation.unchangedBoundaries: Dedicated versus legacy Stripe webhook isolation, owner terms acceptance, strict TEST cohort and LIVE gates remain. New-purchase flags do not disable maintenance of known financial resources. No live billing, service activation or entitlements added.
implementation.limit: The installed storage SDK list/read latency is not a hard hosting wall-clock guarantee. The worker processes at most three records and fences all provider continuation at its deadline, but storage outage timing and actual Netlify execution remain unobserved.
